target_customer: Video creators and marketers (QuickVid, Outpaint phases) and viewers and creators of spatial 3D video (current True3D Labs)
problem: Flat video does not use depth; the company has pursued ways to turn any screen or video into immersive 3D, and in between built tools to repurpose video for short-form and any screen size.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer subscriptions (QuickVid at 10 dollars a month; a directory lists 29 dollars a month for the 3D product, unverified)
product_category: AI video tools and spatial video foundation models

founders.name: Daniel Habib
prior_employers: Meta (Facebook), live video and video infrastructure
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2022-12-30) calls him self-taught and previously at Meta on Facebook Live; YC page says ex-FB engineer with live video, generative AI and VR expertise. Education not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Head-tracked reprojection and AI conversion of 2D video to 3D with depth needs computer vision and real-time graphics; earlier QuickVid was assembled from third-party APIs in weeks, so complexity varied by product.

defensibility.rationale: QuickVid was built from GPT-3, DALL-E 2 and stock video APIs in weeks and was easily copyable; the spatial video models may be harder but no moat evidence is public.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TechCrunch (2022-12) noted Meta and Google had shown text-to-video systems; no source shows a copy or acquisition of True3D.

market_need_then: No source dated near January 2021 describes demand for the founding product; later products targeted short-form video repurposing demand in 2022 and generative AI interest.

branding.domain_note: Uses true3d.com; several unrelated companies have held TRUE3D-style trademarks, and a live TRUE-3D mark belongs to another company.

identity.voice_and_tone: Research lab framing: 'a spatial video lab' and 'what comes after flat video'

branding.community_and_virality: QuickVid received TechCrunch and The Information coverage in December 2022 during the ChatGPT wave; no evidence for the True3D name itself.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic descriptive name shared with unrelated trademarks, with product brands (QuickVid, Outpaint) getting the press instead.

pivots.to: QuickVid, AI tool cutting long videos into short clips
pivots.why: Not stated by a source I read; launched 2022-12-27 as the ChatGPT wave grew.

pivots.to: Outpaint.com, expand any video to fit any screen, including converting UGC ads for connected TV
pivots.why: Not stated; year approximate from YC launch listing, exact date not read.

pivots.to: True3D Labs, research lab building spatial video foundation models and head-tracked 3D playback
pivots.why: Not stated; 80.lv coverage dated 2025-10-02 describes the 3D product.

outcome_analysis: True3D is a very small team led by one former Meta engineer that has moved between products: a 3D video idea at YC, the QuickVid short-form tool launched December 2022, Outpaint for reframing video, and by 2025 a spatial video lab. No funding amounts, revenue or customers were found, so there is no clear success or failure story; it remains active with about five people.
notes: true3d.com returned only a title and the tagline 'A spatial video lab', so the company site gave no content. No funding source found; a directory lists the last stage as Seed with the founder and Travis Kaufman as investors, with no amount, so no round is recorded (unknown, not zero). Competition at founding: no source dated near January 2021 found; 2025 search lists volumetric video firms (Lifecast, Gracia, Arcturus, Volumes, 8i) that are not dated to the batch, so none are listed. The pivot dates are approximate and Outpaint date comes only from a YC listing page title. Whether the 2025 True3D Labs product is the same entity as YC record true3d is assumed from the YC page linking Outpaint and the Habib founder profile.
